Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the chase. South Africa openers Laura Wolvaardt and Tazmin Brits are out to open for the Proteas, while Fatima Sana is ready to bowl the first over of the South African innings.
... The Run Chase ...

As the Proteas prepare to embark on their run chase, the question lingers in the air - Can they successfully chase down the target, or will the Pakistan Women's bowling unit rise to the challenge? The stage is set for a riveting second innings, where every run and wicket will shape the narrative of this encounter. Stay tuned as the first delivery of the second inning is not far away.

After the fall of four wickets, the captain, Fatima Sana, displayed remarkable resilience and forged an impactful partnership of 65 runs with Aliya Riaz. In the 39th over, following the dismissal of Riaz, the wickets began to tumble. However, the captain held her ground, finishing with a commendable 64 runs before being dismissed in the 46th over. At the end of the inning, Ayabonga Khaka, as well as Masabata Klaas, bagged two wickets, and Nadine De Klerk, Tumi Sekhukhune, Chloe Tryon and Annerie Dercksen chipped in for one.

The Pakistan Women's openers started with an aggressive mindset, aiming to put early pressure on their opponents. However, the Proteas bowlers responded well, managing to dismiss both openers. Fortunately, Sidra Amin and Sidra Nawaz steadied the innings, building a solid partnership of 57 runs. Unfortunately, the momentum shifted when Amin retired. This transition took a toll on the team, as Pakistan Women lost two wickets in quick succession.

Pakistan Women have posted a total of 229 runs on the board to challenge the Proteas' batters. The bowling unit delivered an impressive performance, taking down all the opposition batters in just 46 overs. But, is this target set by Pakistan Women enough to secure victory? Only time will reveal the answer!
